subject: red deer
title: Red Deer on a Scottish Island Bite the Heads Off Seabird Chicks

scenes.text: On one Scottish island, red deer bite the heads off baby birds. There's a reason.
The island is Rum, where over 100,000 pairs of Manx shearwaters nest in burrows.
For years, people found shearwater chicks dead, their heads and legs missing.
The killers were red deer. They bite off the heads and chew the legs and wings for the bones.
Scientists think it's about minerals. Rum's plants are low in calcium, and bones are packed with it.
So the deer aren't after meat. They're after the bones.

description:
On the Scottish island of Rum, red deer bite the heads off seabird chicks.
Rum holds one of the world's biggest Manx shearwater colonies, more than 100,000 pairs. A 1988 study in the Journal of Zoology (Furness) reported that red deer there bite the heads off shearwater chicks and sometimes chew the legs and wings to get at the bones, while sheep on Foula in Shetland do the same to tern chicks. The likely reason is mineral deficiency: the island's vegetation is low in calcium, which deer need, for example, to grow antlers.
Did you know plant-eaters sometimes eat meat?
first_comment: Sheep on Foula in Shetland do the same thing to tern chicks. Which plant-eater would surprise you most if it ate meat?
